questions.q: Name the fungal pathogen responsible for the 'bakanae' (foolish seedling) disease of rice and the active substance isolated from it that was later identified as a gibberellin.
questions.a: The fungal pathogen is *Gibberella fujikuroi* and the active substance is gibberellic acid (GA₃). A wrong answer (e.g., naming *Rhizopus* or auxin) reveals the student has not connected the historical discovery to the specific organism and chemical, confusing it with other hormone discoveries.

questions.q: Explain why spraying gibberellins on sugarcane increases yield by up to 20 tonnes per acre, whereas the same treatment on a mature mango tree would not increase fruit size proportionally.
questions.a: Sugarcane stores carbohydrates in its stem; GA-induced internode elongation increases stem volume, allowing more storage capacity. Mango fruit growth is primarily driven by cell division and expansion regulated by auxins and cytokinins during early fruit set; GA application at maturity mainly affects skin elongation, not pulp development. A wrong answer indicates the student cannot differentiate between vegetative growth (stem elongation) and reproductive growth (fruit development) responses to the same hormone.

questions.q: A farmer wants to break dormancy in potato tubers and also induce early flowering in a long-day plant grown under non-inductive short-day conditions. Which single PGR treatment would achieve both, and why?
questions.a: Gibberellins (GA₃) can break tuber dormancy by stimulating hydrolytic enzyme synthesis and also substitute for long-day requirement in some species by promoting flowering. However, cytokinins do not break tuber dormancy. A wrong answer (e.g., cytokinin or ethylene) shows inability to match specific hormone functions to distinct physiological processes (dormancy release vs. flowering induction).

questions.q: Compare the mechanism by which gibberellins and cytokinins each overcome apical dominance in a decapitated shoot.
questions.a: Gibberellins promote elongation of the main shoot, indirectly reducing auxin concentration gradient; cytokinins directly stimulate lateral bud cell division by promoting nutrient mobilisation and synthesising new proteins, overriding auxin's inhibitory signal. A wrong answer conflates the two mechanisms, suggesting both act solely by reducing auxin transport.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Kinetin is a natural cytokinin found in coconut milk and corn kernels." Identify the error and correct it.
questions.a: Kinetin is a synthetic cytokinin derived from autoclaved herring sperm DNA; it does not occur naturally in plants. Natural cytokinins are zeatin (from corn kernels) and cytokinins in coconut milk. A wrong evaluation reveals confusion between the historical discovery compound (kinetin) and naturally occurring cytokinins.

questions.q: Design a simple experiment using two sets of detached bean leaves to demonstrate that cytokinins delay senescence. Specify the control, treatment, measurable parameter, and expected observation after 7 days.
questions.a: Control: leaves in distilled water. Treatment: leaves in 10 ppm kinetin/zeatin solution. Measurable parameter: chlorophyll content (SPAD meter) or visual yellowing score. Expected: treated leaves retain green colour and higher chlorophyll; control leaves yellow. A poor design lacks a control, uses inappropriate concentration, or measures irrelevant parameters (e.g., leaf length).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Gibberellins are a group of over 100 acidic diterpenoid plant growth regulators (denoted GA₁, GA₂, GA₃...) that primarily promote stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering; cytokinins are adenine-derived purine derivatives (e.g., kinetin, zeatin) that specifically stimulate cytokinesis, delay senescence, and promote lateral bud growth by ______ apical dominance.

What is Gibberellins? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Gibberellins are a group of over 100 acidic diterpenoid plant growth regulators (denoted GA₁, GA₂, GA₃...) that primarily promote stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering; cytokinins are adenine-derived purine derivatives (e.g., kinetin, zeatin) that specifically stimulate cytokinesis, delay senescence, and promote lateral bud.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Gibberellins are a group of over ______ acidic diterpenoid plant growth regulators (denoted GA₁, GA₂, GA₃...) that primarily promote stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering; cytokinins are adenine-derived purine derivatives (e.g., kinetin, zeatin) that specifically stimulate cytokinesis, delay senescence, and promote lateral bud growth by counteracting apical dominance.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can explain the distinct physiological roles of gibberellins and cytokinins with specific examples, describe their discovery history, and predict the outcome of their application or deficiency in agricultural scenarios (e.g., bolting in rosette plants, delaying leaf senescence in cut flowers).
